policy: Fast-moving work enters this registry before stable chapters. An entry records source claims and book relevance, not an independent reproduction.

entries.title: Dreamer 4: Training Agents Inside of Scalable World Models
entries.problem: Scale a video world model far enough to train a behavior in imagination while retaining interactive action-conditioned rollout speed.
entries.why_it_matters: It connects the stable RSSM and imagination-learning chapters to a transformer-scale successor and exposes the difference between inference speed and training feasibility.
entries.resource_path: S tier audits the paper and interfaces only; model training or checkpoint execution remains an optional L path and is not a reading prerequisite.
entries.scope_boundary: The paper reports Minecraft results and single-GPU interactive inference; neither statement establishes 24 GB training feasibility or robot and driving validity.
review_triggers: A new paper version changes the architecture or reported evaluation scope.
Official runnable assets expose a resource profile that can be audited without inventing results.

entries.title: V-JEPA 2.1: Dense Video Predictive Representations
entries.problem: Learn dense spatial and temporal video representations without making pixel reconstruction the only predictive objective.
entries.why_it_matters: It sharpens the book's separation between representation prediction, state readability and action-conditioned transition evidence.
entries.resource_path: S tier uses the chapter's analytic probe; optional M work may audit frozen features, while full upstream training remains outside the default resource route.
entries.scope_boundary: Author-reported dense and robot results do not prove that a frozen feature contains every control state or supports counterfactual planning in this book.
review_triggers: The official repository changes checkpoints, licenses or dense-feature interfaces.
A peer-reviewed venue or independent reproduction changes the evidence maturity.

entries.title: NVIDIA Cosmos 3 Unified Physical-AI Generation Interface
entries.problem: Expose text, vision, sound and action through a common world-generation platform for multiple physical-AI use cases.
entries.why_it_matters: It is a useful open interface case for teaching why action support, simulator fidelity and downstream control validity remain separate claims.
entries.resource_path: S tier audits the repository contract and declared limitations; any checkpoint, data or post-training run is optional and must first pass license and resource checks.
entries.scope_boundary: An official unified action interface does not independently validate action-state consistency, 3D structure, physical plausibility, policy ranking or safety.
review_triggers: The repository changes model generations, action schemas, licenses or limitation statements.
A smaller frozen checkpoint becomes feasible within a measured optional resource tier.

entries.title: WorldArena 2.0 Embodied World-Model Benchmark
entries.problem: Extend world-model evaluation across modalities, downstream functions and simulated plus real robotic platforms.
entries.why_it_matters: It reinforces the book's evidence ladder from visual perception through interactive utility while making protocol and platform scope explicit.
entries.resource_path: S tier compares benchmark contracts and claim scopes; running models, visuotactile data or real platforms is optional and remains unverified here.
entries.scope_boundary: The benchmark proposal and public page describe intended coverage; this book has not run the assets and does not adopt its aggregate score as universal validity.
review_triggers: A new benchmark version changes modality, functionality, platform or aggregation scope.
Public assets and protocol files become sufficiently complete for an independent audit.

entries.title: KineBench IDM-Free Kinematic Grounding
entries.problem: Reduce attribution ambiguity when generated videos must be converted into executable robot motion for closed-loop evaluation.
entries.why_it_matters: It provides a concrete evaluator-of-evaluator example: pose extraction and kinematic grounding are measured components rather than invisible plumbing.
entries.resource_path: S tier uses the attribution lesson in Chapter 9; executing the cascaded vision models and ManiSkill3 suites remains optional and unverified.
entries.scope_boundary: Replacing an inverse dynamics model with pose extraction reduces one ambiguity but does not make the extractor error-free or prove real-world physical validity.
review_triggers: The accepted paper receives a revision or official artifact release.
Independent studies quantify pose-extraction error separately from world-model error.

entries.title: GE-Sim 2.0 Closed-Loop Video World Simulator
entries.problem: Combine action-conditioned video rollout, decoded state, learned outcome scoring and faster inference for robot-policy learning and evaluation.
entries.why_it_matters: It is a compact case for tracing three distinct error sources: learned transition, state expert and world judge, before trusting policy updates.
entries.resource_path: S tier audits the component graph and reported protocol; the paper's H100 inference setting is not a default experiment or local measurement.
entries.scope_boundary: Leaderboard position, author-reported real gains and H100 speed remain paper results; they do not establish independent calibration or 24 GB feasibility.
review_triggers: Official code, weights, data or evaluator definitions are released.
Independent robot outcomes test whether simulator rankings hold for new policies and tasks.

entries.title: Interactive World Simulator for Policy Training and Evaluation
entries.problem: Use consistency models for faster long-horizon robot interaction and then compare world-model-trained or evaluated policies with real outcomes.
entries.why_it_matters: It directly targets the book's simulator-utility question and shows why throughput, long-horizon stability and real-policy ranking need separate evidence.
entries.resource_path: S tier records the evaluation design; reported RTX 4090 throughput and real-robot comparisons remain upstream measurements, not local resource results.
entries.scope_boundary: Long generated rollouts and author-reported correlation do not guarantee calibrated absolute success, unseen-policy ranking or safety outside the evaluated tasks.
review_triggers: Runnable artifacts expose the exact data, policy population and real-evaluation protocol.
A later revision changes the reported throughput, duration or generalization scope.

entries.title: OSCAR Cross-Embodiment Action-Conditioned World Model
entries.problem: Represent actions across robot embodiments with a shared visual skeleton condition for world-model policy evaluation.
entries.why_it_matters: It gives the cross-embodiment chapter a concrete hypothesis while preserving the distinction between representational alignment and executable action semantics.
entries.resource_path: S tier compares action-schema hypotheses; the reported GH200 fine-tuning path is outside the default 24 GB route and is not required for reading.
entries.scope_boundary: A 2D skeleton can align visible kinematics but does not by itself encode force, contact, actuator limits, latency or invertible control across embodiments.
review_triggers: Official assets expose the skeleton renderer, data mixtures or policy-evaluation protocol.
Independent cross-embodiment tests separate visual alignment from executable control transfer.
